ctl.tip: Input gain in dB, before everything else. The shaper reacts to level changes, not to the absolute level, so this mainly sets how hard the threshold and the limiter are hit. Double-click for 0.
ctl.label: Input dB

ctl.tip: Number of bands: 1 to 4. Each band shapes its own part of the sound. Drag the vertical dividers in the graph to place the crossovers. Unused bands are greyed out.
Crossover slope: how steeply the bands are separated, from 12 to 96 dB per octave. Default 24. Steeper keeps bands cleaner but rings a little more. The bands always add back flat.

ctl.tip: Hear the shaped result, as it will leave the plugin (Mix applies).
Hear only the attack part of the shaped sound: the shaped sound minus its sustain part. Mix is ignored while listening.
Hear only the sustain part of the shaped sound (what is left after the attack part is taken away). Mix is ignored while listening.
Mix: shaped sound against the untouched input (delayed to match, so there is no comb filtering). 100% is fully shaped, 0% is exactly the input.
ctl.label: Mix

ctl.tip: Normal range (default).
Double: Attack and Sustain push twice as many dB per percent.
Four times: extreme shaping. Raise Max dB on a band to let it go further. The limiter still holds the Ceiling.
Spectrum behind the bands. In + Out shows the input in grey and the output in green. The scale on the right is dBFS.

ctl.tip: Output gain in dB, after the Mix and before the limiter, so you can push the sound into the limiter. Double-click for 0.

ctl.tip: Limiter ceiling in dB, -12 to 0. Nothing leaves the plugin above this level. Default -0.3.
ctl.label: Ceil

ctl.tip: Limiter on or off. A lookahead limiter at the very end: nothing leaves the plugin above the Ceiling, whatever the Mix.
Limiter release in ms: how fast the limiter lets go after a peak. Used when Auto is off. 5 to 500 ms.
ctl.label: Release

ctl.tip: Auto release: the limiter lets go slowly after a hard hit and quickly after a light one. Switch it off to set the release by hand.
Lookahead in ms, 1 to 7.5 (default 3). The limiter sees peaks this long before they play, so it can turn down smoothly. Longer is cleaner, shorter is lower latency. It sets the reported latency.
ctl.label: Look

Level before the shaper (after the Input gain below). Two bars, left and right, in dB: the bar is the average level, the white line is the peak. Blue is safe, purple is the warning zone, pink is clipping. The cap stays pink after a clip; click to clear it.

Frequency view, 20 Hz to 20 kHz. Drag the vertical dividers to move the crossovers. The coloured line in each band is the gain the shaper applies right now (left scale, -12 to +12 dB). Right scale: spectrum in dBFS.

Transient picture of this band. Scope: red is the original band, green is the shaped band, grey is where they overlap, as a waveform shape in dB over the last seconds. Gain: how much the band was turned up or down over time, in dB. Choose with the buttons below; Zoom changes the time span.

Load your own audio file for the preview. Nothing is uploaded; it is decoded in this page only.

Preview level (preview only). Quiet: as generated. Loud: up to 6 dB hotter, peaks kept at -1 dB. Mastered: peaks at -0.5 dB, like a finished track. No level ever clips the rig or tickles the master limiter on its own, so 0% Mix is the untouched sound. The Input gain knob of the plugin does the same job on your own music.

Level match (preview only): the shaped sound is turned up or down to the same average loudness as the dry sound, so A/B (B key) compares punch and sustain instead of volume. Uses a 0.5 s average. Loops play at 150 BPM.

other.tip: Live comparison of the shaped sound against the dry input (after input gain), averaged over about half a second. RMS: average level change in dB. Crest: peak minus RMS, dry then shaped. LU at equal peak: how much louder the shaped sound can be played before its peak reaches the dry peak (dry crest minus shaped crest). Mix and Level match show up here.
